response.markdown_report:
**Select a controlled negative-sampling intervention for NextItNet.** At 0% progress, changing one training component offers a practical accuracy experiment while retaining the existing diagnostic adapter.

**Insights from the supplied evidence.** (1) Uniform training-audit HR@10 reaches 0.9362–0.9953, while frequency-weighted competitors reduce it in every category. This supports testing competitor selection, but fitted-target performance does not establish generalization. (2) Recent-history ablation changes margins more than older-history ablation. This demonstrates model sensitivity; it does not establish current intent or justify removing older events. (3) Numerical-reference discrepancies and unavailable predictor reload checks limit correctness claims. In-memory scoring agreement cannot establish generated-predictor parity.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Negative-sampling experiments [1] report sampler-dependent popularity effects and frequency-group disparities. Therefore, evaluate a sampling intervention separately across categories and training-frequency bands. (2) gBCE [2] identifies confidence problems associated with sampled BCE. Consequently, larger margins alone should not select a model, and changing the loss simultaneously would obscure attribution. (3) Interaction-removal research [3] motivates perturbation sensitivity checks. Such checks remain descriptive because altered histories can introduce artifacts.

The framework separates three directions:

| Direction | Existing evidence | Proposed action | Decision evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| Competitive discrimination | Frequency-sensitive training ranks | Change negative distribution | Pinned validation HR@10 |
| Optimization stability | Sampled-loss concerns [2] | Test calibrated loss separately | Validation plus finite-loss checks |
| Temporal specificity | Recent-history sensitivity | Controlled order audit | Supported paired score changes |

Three atomic ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation.

| Idea | Scores | Originality: positive / negative | Potential: positive / negative | Difficulty: positive / negative |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| **50% uniform, 50% frequency^0.75 negatives** [1] | **3/6/2** | Diagnostic-driven / established sampler | Direct learning intervention / possible popularity distortion | Small sampler change / eligibility handling |
| gBCE loss substitution [2] | 3/6/4 | Backbone-compatible transfer / existing loss | Confidence control / uncertain ranking benefit | Local loss change / requires exact parameterization |
| Matched recent-versus-older order swaps [3] | 4/5/5 | Controlled comparison / established perturbations | Clarifies dependence / no direct accuracy mechanism | Frozen-model reuse / support matching complexity |

**Chosen experiment.** Compute occurrence counts exclusively from training histories. For each baseline negative slot, choose uniform or count^0.75 sampling with equal probability, restricted to the baseline-authorized negative pool. Keep negative count, loss, optimizer, architecture and update schedule fixed; apply no importance correction, explicitly testing the changed training objective.

Train one NextItNet per category from the supplied corrected cold start. Preserve seeds, all four routes, 200 batches/epoch, at most 200 epochs, trial-local artifacts and the single-GPU budget. Compare once using host-reported macro validation HR@10; report category outcomes without claiming unseen results. Retain the diagnostic interfaces and final-nonpadding readout. Inference remains unchanged, with exactly one checkpoint per category.

idea.description: Test a fixed 50% uniform and 50% training-frequency^0.75 negative-sampling distribution in the corrected NextItNet baseline, changing no other training component and deploying one independently trained checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: The supplied fitted-training audit shows lower target hit rates against frequency-weighted competitors in every category. This motivates a narrowly controlled training experiment; it does not demonstrate that popularity-weighted training will improve pinned validation HR@10. At the initial research stage, a small sampler change is more feasible than expanding the already substantial diagnostic machinery.
idea.implementation_notes:
Use the supplied corrected NextItNet cold start independently for Movies_and_TV, Industrial_and_Scientific, Electronics and CDs_and_Vinyl. Compute category-specific item occurrence counts from training interactions only, retaining repeated events. For each negative slot, draw a Bernoulli(0.5) component, then sample from the baseline-authorized eligible pool: uniformly for one component, proportionally to count^0.75 for the other. Rejection sampling from a category alias table is acceptable when it produces this conditional weighted distribution; if an operational rejection limit is reached, sample exactly from eligible weights rather than silently switching distributions. If all eligible weights are zero, use uniform sampling and record the fallback. Preserve the baseline's duplicate policy; when distinct negatives are required, remove already selected IDs and renormalize at each draw. Never sample padding, reserved IDs, the supervised positive, or baseline-excluded user positives. Do not inspect validation or test interactions to define eligibility. Counts are sampler inputs only and never contribute inference scores.

Keep the baseline negative count, loss, optimizer, architecture, batch size, checkpoint-selection rule and all other hyperparameters fixed. Apply no importance correction: the intervention deliberately changes the negative term's training expectation, so it is not an unbiased estimator of the original uniform-negative objective. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per epoch. DATA_DIR must remain os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR']; write artifacts beneath the current trial directory. Train on one GPU within the shared 43,200 GPU-second search budget. Do not read other trials or reuse their checkpoints. Predeclare this configuration before further validation exposure and use only the host's unchanged pinned macro validation HR@10 for selection. Retain the baseline's existing checkpoint-selection procedure and record its validation exposure.

Keep the architecture and generated predictor writer unchanged and consistent, loading exactly one NextItNet checkpoint per category without averaging or score fusion. Preserve log2feats(sequence), item_emb, predict_score(features, items), all ModelView fields, DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), and diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis). Final features must come from the largest nonzero sequence index, with all-padding rows explicitly excluded. Diagnostics must return metrics and metric_definitions, finite-support counts and explicit unavailable statuses. Use fixed diagnostic candidate manifests when a host-supported mechanism exists; diagnostic-local RNGs must not change training RNG state. Report actual sampler component counts, fallback counts, supported frequency-band results and elapsed diagnostic cost. Keep training audits, qualitative simulator feedback and pinned validation evidence separate. Predictor reload parity remains unavailable unless actually checked through a supplied interface. No unavailable reviews, ratings, item attributes or simulator traits are required.
idea.pseudocode:
counts = training_occurrence_counts(category_histories)
weighted_sampler = build_alias_table(counts ** 0.75)
rng = baseline_training_rng(seed=42)

for epoch in baseline_epoch_schedule(maximum=200):
    for batch_index in range(200):
        users, sequence, positive = baseline_sample_training_examples(rng)
        negative = baseline_negative_tensor_shape(positive)
        for slot in baseline_valid_negative_slots(sequence, positive):
            eligible = baseline_authorized_negative_pool(users, slot)
            eligible = apply_baseline_duplicate_policy(eligible, negative, slot)
            if rng.random() < 0.5:
                negative[slot] = uniform_sample(eligible, rng)
            else:
                negative[slot] = exact_conditional_weighted_sample(
                    eligible, counts ** 0.75, weighted_sampler, rng,
                    zero_weight_fallback='uniform_and_record')
        features = model.log2feats(sequence)
        loss = unchanged_baseline_loss(features, positive, negative)
        unchanged_optimizer_step(loss)
    apply_existing_checkpoint_selection_rule()

# Repeat independently for all four category routes.
# Preserve the corrected predictor writer and one checkpoint/category.
# Host independently reports pinned per-category and macro validation HR@10.
# Diagnostic final readout:
positions = arange(sequence.shape[1]).expand_as(sequence)
last = where(sequence != 0, positions, -1).amax(dim=1)
valid = last >= 0
final_features = features[valid, last[valid]]

originality.positive: Connects the measured frequency-competitor gap to a minimal, predeclared NextItNet intervention with an interpretable single-component comparison.
originality.negative: Uniform/popularity mixture sampling and the 0.75 exponent are established techniques; the contribution is task-specific experimental design.

future_potential.positive: Provides a cheap direct test of whether competitive-negative exposure improves held-out ranking and supports later frequency-stratified loss research.
future_potential.negative: Popularity weighting can distort the objective, amplify ambiguous-negative effects and reduce uniform-candidate performance; training-audit gains may not transfer.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires a count table and a sampler change while preserving architecture, checkpoint format, predictor and diagnostic contracts.
code_difficulty.negative: Conditional eligibility, zero-weight pools, duplicate policies and deterministic sampling require care; executable integration depends on the supplied baseline sampler.

related_work.title: Negative-sampling experiments (2024), supplied search result
contributions: Reports sampler-dependent popularity effects and differences across head, middle and tail item groups.
Motivates reporting frequency-stratified outcomes alongside aggregate ranking results.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed fixed mixture improves this NextItNet benchmark.
Aggregate findings do not identify which unobserved items are true negatives.

related_work.title: gBCE (2024), supplied search result
contributions: Addresses confidence and training issues associated with sampled binary cross-entropy.
Motivates separating loss behavior from ranking evaluation.
limitations: A loss intervention would require a separate controlled experiment.
Confidence calibration alone does not establish improved pinned HR@10.

related_work.title: Betello et al., ECIR 2024, supplied interaction-removal study
contributions: Examines recommendation sensitivity to removal of historical interactions.
limitations: Removal changes the observed history and can introduce perturbation artifacts.
Sensitivity does not establish causal interest decay, current intent or validation improvement.
